intent: review_loop.sh runs gate, review and repair without a human. implement() hands the fixer prompt (agents/fixer.md followed by the findings) to the configured implementer, Claude or Codex. A repair round must either change code or record responses; a tool failure must never pass as a repair round.
note: A bug this kit once had: agents/fixer.md starts with '---' frontmatter; passed as the argument of `claude -p` the CLI read it as an option and errored, so the Claude implementer never ran and the loop re-reviewed the same commit until the round cap. Rebuilt by reversing the fix: base is the fixed script without its explanatory comment and without the failure guards the fix added (the shipped script had none either), head is the script as shipped, so the diff is the one line that introduced the bug. Adjudicated by the author of the fix. On its first run, the reviewer flagged the argument bug and, separately, that implement()'s exit status is ignored at both call sites so a never-started implementer passes as a repair round. That is the guard the fix added, so both findings are expected.

base.code_quality/scripts/review_loop.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Autonomous gate → cross-model review → repair loop. No human in the loop
# until it either converges (prints an evidence packet) or hits the round cap
# (prints an escalation packet). Run it on a feature branch with commits.
#
#   review_loop.sh [--base origin/main] [--intent "task / acceptance criteria"] [--depth deep]
#
# Exit: 0 converged · 1 gate never went green · 3 round cap hit (human needed) · 2 tool error
set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
KIT="$(dirname "$HERE")"
ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"; cd "$ROOT"
BASE="origin/main"; INTENT=""; DEPTH=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --base) BASE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --intent) INTENT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --depth) DEPTH="--depth $2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) echo "unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
export QUALITY_BASE="$BASE"
STATE="$ROOT/.quality"; mkdir -p "$STATE"; [ -f "$STATE/.gitignore" ] || echo '*' > "$STATE/.gitignore"

cfg() { python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'$HERE'); import qlib; c=qlib.load_config(); print($1)"; }
IMPL="$(cfg 'c["agents"]["implementer"]')"
MAX_ROUNDS="$(cfg 'c["review"].get("max_rounds",3)')"
DIFF_ONLY_AFTER="$(cfg 'c["review"].get("diff_only_after_round",2)')"
CLAUDE_MODEL="$(cfg 'c["agents"]["claude_model"]')"
CODEX_MODEL="$(cfg 'c["agents"]["codex_model"]')"
# Implementer permissions. Run the loop in a worktree/sandbox; override if your setup differs.
CLAUDE_IMPL_ARGS="${CLAUDE_IMPL_ARGS:---permission-mode auto}"

implement() {  # $1 = prompt
  if [ "$IMPL" = "codex" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$1" | codex exec -m "$CODEX_MODEL" -s workspace-write --ephemeral -
  else
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    printf '%s' "$1" | claude -p --model "$CLAUDE_MODEL" $CLAUDE_IMPL_ARGS
  fi
}

commit_if_dirty() {  # reviews read commits, so every repair must be committed
  if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- . ':!.quality')" ]; then
    git add -A -- . ':!.quality' && git commit -q -m "$1"
  fi
}

gate_until_green() {  # up to 3 repair attempts for deterministic failures
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    if out="$("$HERE/quality_gate.sh" full 2>&1)"; then echo "$out"; return 0; fi
    echo "$out" | tail -n 80
    echo "── gate failed (attempt $attempt) — handing errors to $IMPL"
    implement "$(cat "$KIT/agents/fixer.md")

## Deterministic gate failures (fix these first)
\`\`\`
$(echo "$out" | tail -n 150)
\`\`\`"
    commit_if_dirty "review-loop: fix gate failures (attempt $attempt)"
  done
  "$HERE/quality_gate.sh" full
}

: > "$STATE/rounds.log"
rm -f "$STATE/ledger.json" "$STATE/responses.json"
last_reviewed=""
for round in $(seq 1 "$MAX_ROUNDS"); do
  echo "═══ Round $round/$MAX_ROUNDS"
  gate_until_green || { echo "Gate still red after repairs."; exit 1; }

  since=""
  if [ "$round" -ge "$DIFF_ONLY_AFTER" ] && [ -n "$last_reviewed" ]; then since="--since $last_reviewed"; fi
  head_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  python3 "$HERE/cross_review.py" --base "$BASE" $since $DEPTH --intent "$INTENT"
  rc=$?
  echo "round=$round sha=$head_sha rc=$rc" >> "$STATE/rounds.log"
  last_reviewed="$head_sha"

  if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then
    python3 "$HERE/classify_risk.py" --base "$BASE" --model > /dev/null
    python3 "$HERE/evidence_packet.py" --base "$BASE" --rounds "$round" --status converged
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ $rc -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "Review incomplete (rc=$rc): a reviewer or verifier failed — see .quality/review.md. Not a code problem; fix the tooling and re-run."
    exit 2
  fi

  [ "$round" -eq "$MAX_ROUNDS" ] && break
  implement "$(cat "$KIT/agents/fixer.md")

## Verified findings (round $round)
$(cat "$STATE/review.md")"
  commit_if_dirty "review-loop: address round $round findings"
  if [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$head_sha" ]; then
    echo "Implementer made no code changes; re-reviewing with its responses."
  fi
done

python3 "$HERE/classify_risk.py" --base "$BASE" --model > /dev/null
python3 "$HERE/evidence_packet.py" --base "$BASE" --rounds "$MAX_ROUNDS" --status escalated
exit 3
base.code_quality/agents/fixer.md:
---
name: fixer
description: Implementer prompt used by the review loop to address verified findings. Not a reviewer.
---
You are the implementer. Independent reviewers from another model family
raised the verified findings below on your change. Address every one:

- Fix it. Fix the whole bug class, not just the cited line: search for every
  other instance and fix those too.
- Or, if you are certain it is wrong or intentional, do not change code for it.
  Append an entry to `.quality/responses.json` (a JSON list) of the form
  {"file": "...", "bug_class": "...", "reason": "..."} with a concrete,
  code-backed reason. A verifier will check your reason; "intentional" alone
  will be rejected.
- For an "unresolved" finding, the fastest way to settle it is a test that
  exercises the failure scenario. If the test passes, keep it and say so in
  your response entry. If it fails, fix the bug.

Constraints:
- Keep the repair minimal. No unrelated refactors or cleanups in a repair round.
- Never weaken a check to make it pass (delete/skip tests, loosen assertions,
  add suppressions, lower thresholds, regenerate snapshots blindly).
- Run the full quality gate (`code_quality/scripts/quality_gate.sh full`) and
  show the tail of its output before you finish.
- Commit your changes with a message that lists the finding ids you addressed.
